learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of advanced pydantic models in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to field metadata and descriptions.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers advanced pydantic models within request data and pydantic models. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use advanced pydantic models to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is clear input/output contracts, field validation, serialization and safe defaults.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Advanced Pydantic Models matters because it is part of request data and pydantic models. In practice, focus on clear input/output contracts, field validation, serialization and safe defaults. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Field metadata and descriptions
items.text: For field metadata and descriptions, define the accepted shape and constraints explicitly. Validate untrusted input at the boundary, distinguish omitted values from explicit nulls, and return only fields the caller is allowed to see.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Advanced Pydantic Models
content_blocks.expected_output: POST /products with {"name":"Notebook","price":2.5} returns validated JSON; price <= 0 is rejected.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run with fastapi dev main.py; use /docs to submit a valid and an invalid body.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.
content_blocks.limitations: This code is inspectable lesson material, not executed by CodeLeaf. Run it only in a local virtual environment or a separately isolated runner with resource/time/network limits. Security examples are sketches, not complete production authentication or authorization systems.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Adapt the example to cover “Field metadata and descriptions”. Write down the expected success result and one invalid, missing, duplicate, timeout or permission-boundary case that matters for this topic.

task: Create a small reviewable artifact for “Advanced Pydantic Models”: explain its goal, cover the listed subtopics, show an example with expected result, then include one edge case and how you would verify it.
hints: Start with “Field metadata and descriptions” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Advanced Pydantic Models, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.
